- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) and model forecast is flat or trending down, adjust upward by 2–5% to account for sentiment-driven momentum.
- After a sharp price spike (true outcome > 75), model tends to overcorrect; reduce forecast slope by 10–20% for next 5–7 days to avoid overshoot.
- If official event net supply is negative and bullish events outnumber bearish, model underestimates upside; add 3–8% bias to forecast mean.
- If sentiment history shows repeated bearish swings (e.g., -0.33, -0.50) and model is flat, introduce slight downward drift (0.5–1.5% per day) to reflect mean reversion.
- For 30-day forecasts with high event count and negative supply net, model often underestimates volatility; increase forecast range by 10–15% to capture event-driven swings.
- When sentiment is mixed or neutral (0.00–0.33) and model is trending, reduce forecast slope to avoid overconfidence in direction.
- If recent auction supply events are frequent (≥3/30d) and model is flat, assume short-term volatility; add ±2% noise to forecast to reflect auction-driven noise.
